newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - 144a for Thailand's IFCT.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - 144a for Thailand's IFCT.

text.p: International Finance Corp of Thailand's US$200 million 144a bond was the big deal on Friday, but Indonesia's Lippo Bank also came through with a US$50 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue.
IFCT's 7.375-percent bond due in 2007 was priced and re-offered at 99.624 to yield 7.429 percent or 90 basis points over the 6.5-percent, 10-year U.S. Treasury note due October 2006.
Merrill Lynch was lead manager and bookrunner. Lehman Brothers, JP Morgan and Salomon Brothers were co-managers.
IFCT's foreign currency debt is rated equally with the sovereign at A2 by Moody's Investors Service and Single-A by Standard and Poor's Corp.
As a result, the issue is expected to set a benchmark for future Thai issues. Last April, IFCT set a seven-year bond that yielded about 70 basis points over the U.S. benchmark.
Bankers deemed the latest issue a success, especially given the political and financial woes in Thailand that have driven the country's stock market sharply lower.
"It's a terrific comeback for Thailand," said a manager at Merrill Lynch, adding that IFCT has been very pleased with the response to the issue.
Analysts noted that Thailand recently has taken steps to get the economy back on track that are likely to impress foreign investors.
Asian bankers predict that Thai Farmers Bank will be the next Thai issuer to come to the market.

Thai Farmers Bank said in late December that it had mandated ABN Amro to arrange a US$125 million five-year financing that will carry a margin of 27 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
Indonesia's Lippo Bank today launched a US$50 million FRCD via arrangers Arab Banking Corp Singapore, BNP Singapore, LTCB Asia and Tokai Asia.
The certificates mature in four years but can be put after two. The pay a coupon of 80 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in return of 101 basis points to top-tier managers.

The issue is priced wider than some recent Indonesian FRCDs, which some bankers said could help the deal's syndication. They said the FRCDs also have some rarity value because Lippo is an infrequent issuer.

Bankers said the row over contributions made to the U.S. Democratic party by individuals linked to the Lippo Group could dissuade some banks from signing on to the deal, but the scandal's effect on the issue is likely to be mild.
"Some people might be worried about what is going on," said a syndicate manager.
In other news, Merrill Lynch held a roadshow for the upcoming subordinated bond issue for Hong Kong's Dao Heng Bank, which is expected to be launched by the end of January.

Standard and Poor's Corp assigned a BB-plus rating to two proposed 144a unsecured note issues of India's Reliance Industries--a US$100 million century bond and a US$214 million 30-year bond that can be put after 10 years.

Merrill Lynch, which is focusing more attention on India this year, is tipped to lead the Reliance deal. Lehman Brothers and Merrill Lynch will lead a US$750 million Euro-Asian floating rate note for Ford Credit next week that will be targetted at Asian investors. Ford Credit launched a US$750 million fixed rate Euro-Asian bond in May 1996.
